newsitem.title: GERMANY: West European cotton buyers emerge at lower prices.
newsitem.headline: West European cotton buyers emerge at lower prices.

text.p: European spinning mills appeared in the market after prices had eased continuously throughout August and as the holiday period drew to an end, the Bremen Cotton Exchange's fortnightly report said on Monday.
It said consumers needed to buy significant amounts of raw materials and felt encouraged by a softer dollar versus the mark.
Cotton stocks held in Bremen on August 23 were down at 58,512 versus 89,665 a month earlier but compared with 48,331 a a year ago.

Reported trades included Central Asian cottons 1 and 2 and West African description for dates up to Sept/Oct 1997, Paraguay cotton for the present quarter, as well as Zimbabwe and Greek high grades for the fourth quarter of 1996.
Extralongstaple markets saw transactions in Israel-Pima, U.S.-Pima and Peru-Pima/Del Cerro for fourth quarter 1996 through first quarter 1997.
